text:
The $ANT IPO was solid.

1) For the company, the IPO was great. They raised more money than they original thought with the both the amount of shares offered and IPO price increased.

2) The stock closed up 17% which is above the 10-15% threshold to call an IPO of this size successful.

3) The not so great news is the stock opened at +34% peaked a few minutes thereafter at +39% and then closed at +17%. A successful IPO sees the stock close higher than the open. This shows that investors who did not get an allocation are more eager to buy than those looking to sell the initial IPO pop and in this case, now that they finally have liquidity.

4) This decline in Anthropic’s stock over the day is likely the cause of the S&P going from up 1.3% in the morning to flat at the 11:49AM open of the IPO to down 2.0% by the close.

5) The real test of whether this was a successful IPO will come over the next 30 days during the green shoe window. Does the stock stays above its $83 IPO price in a tough tape for AI related stocks? I am not so sure.

Longer-term positives for Anthropic:

1) The value of frontier models increased with the US mid-term election of more pro regulatory politicians.

2) The CEO of $NVDA was the biggest proponent of open-weight models. With him gone, the potential for regulatory capture by Anthropic and OpenAI increases.

3) Anthropic was focused on day one on enterprises who are willing to pay vs OpenAI that focused on consumers who are used to getting internet services for free like search.

4) There is scarcity value in Anthropic being the first pureplay LLM that investors have and it is likely to be fast tracked into the indices.

5) The total available market of knowledge work was estimated at $40 trillion in 2025.

Negatives:

1) Combined revenue growth for OpenAI and Anthropic are slowing from ~75% q/q in Q2 to ~50% in Q3

2) Price competition between OAI, Anthropic and open-weight seems to be increasing. OAI price cuts drove revenue growth from roughly 17% q/q in Q2 to 50% in Q3 but dropped Anthropic from 144% q/q to 47%. But both saw adjusted operating margins going lower as a result. Anthropic dropped from 19% in Q2 to 15% in Q3 while OAI losses increased from roughly $10.1B to $10.9B in Q3. Combined operating losses increased from roughly $7.9B in Q2 to $8.4B in Q3.

3) Open-weight models are good for 90%+ of tasks today and they are likely to only get better. Harnesses are increasingly being used. They pick the best model for the task which in most cases is open-weight. This is why cost per token has come down by over 60% since May though this has driven tokens up nearly 6x.

4) I believe that ultimately enterprises will gravitate towards the safety of the $MSFT ecosystem while consumers will access AI on their smartphones either through the iOS ($AAPL) or Android ($GOOGL) ecosystems. 

5) The end-users are likely to become indifferent to which model is picked to run their tasks which then would commoditize this LLM layer over time.

In summary: price competition is increasing, rev growth is slowing and operating margins are dropping for the two leading LLMs while capital commitments are massive. But the opportunity is massive as well and Agentic AI is in its nascency. If I had to pick one LLM that survives the commoditization of this layer, Anthropic would be it. But it is not a favorite of mine for AI overall in the near-term.

text:
This is quite interesting seeing project like @solflare launched Private Mode powered by @Helius , enabling encrypted private balances and payments directly within the same Solana wallet address without needing a separate wallet.

Private balances are computed on the user's device from encrypted records, with zero knowledge proofs allowing Solana to verify transactions while hiding asset types and amounts between enabled users.

Sender and receiver addresses plus deposit/withdrawal amounts remain visible on-chain, while swaps, staking, and dApps continue using the public balance.

Here’s a simple, beginner-friendly explanation of Solflare Private Mode.

On Solana like most blockchains, everything is public by default, if someone has your wallet address, they can look it up and see exactly how much SOL, USDC, or any token you hold, plus every amount you’ve sent or received. 

This is useful for transparency, but it also means your landlord, boss, ex, or random people online can see your full financial activity.

 What Private Mode does ?
Private Mode adds a private balance right next to your normal public balance on the same wallet address, you don’t need a second wallet.

Think of it like this:  
Your Solana wallet is normally a transparent glass jar, anyone can look inside and see exactly how much money is in it and how much you move around.  

Private Mode adds a locked black box inside that same jar, people can still see the jar and that you moved money into or out of the black box, and they can see who you handed a package to, but they can’t see how much is inside the box or how much was in the package.

Simple example (Alice pays Bob).

1. Alice has 100 USDC in her normal (public) Solflare balance.

2. She turns on Private Mode and moves 50 USDC into her private balance, this deposit is public, anyone looking at the blockchain sees “Alice deposited 50 USDC into Private Mode.

3. Now Alice’s private balance shows 50 USDC only to her, public block explorers cannot see this amount.

4. She sends 20 USDC privately to Bob who also has Private Mode turned on.

   → Everyone can see “Alice sent something to Bob, but they cannot see that it was 20 USDC, or even that it was USDC, the amount and the token type are hidden.

5. Bob receives the 20 USDC in his private balance, only he can see it.

6. If Alice later wants to swap, stake, or use a dApp, she moves the money back to her public balance, that withdrawal amount becomes public again.

What people can still see:
Who sent to whom.
When the transaction happened.
That a wallet is using Private Mode.
The amount and token of private payments between Private Mode users.

What stays hidden:
Your private balance amount.
Which tokens are in your private balance.
Deposit and withdrawal amounts.

Key points for beginners
- Same address, same keys fully self-custodial. Solflare and Helius never hold your funds, you stay in control the whole time.

- It uses zero knowledge proofs, a type of math so the Solana network can confirm the payment is valid without revealing the numbers.

- It only works for private payments between people who both have Private Mode enabled, sending to someone without it becomes a normal public transfer.

- In the current version, swaps, staking, and most dApps still use your public balance.

Private Mode doesn’t make you invisible it hides how much you have and how much you send, while still letting the blockchain verify everything at normal Solana speed. 

It’s a practical middle ground between full public transparency and stronger privacy tools.

Privacy Rings went live on Solana mainnet on November 10. Here is what that changes for a trader.

Before Rings, a position on Solana sat in a wallet's token accounts. Anyone with your address could open it and read the coin, the size and when you got in. Trackers, holder lists and bag checks all read that one place.

Rings add a second place to hold a coin: a shielded pool program by @Helius where balances are encrypted on chain and only your viewing key reads them. Every transaction still needs your wallet's signature.

Anon is a terminal on top of it. A buy takes SOL out of the pool, swaps it on a route from Jupiter and puts the coins back in the pool, in one transaction your wallet signs.

What changes:
1. A balance read of your wallet doesn't show what you hold in the pool
2. A holder list shows one line for the pool's vault, and your pool holdings don't sit under your wallet
3. A send to another Anon user encrypts the coin and the amount

What stays public: your wallet on every deposit, trade and withdrawal, and every amount in or out of the pool.
